items.a: It’s Tagalog for “new life”. Kim chose it because her mission is to give old materials new life.
Kim. Every piece is made by her, by hand, in small batches.
100% second-hand fabric — from estate sales, Goodwill, friends’ closets, a second-hand kimono shop in Japan, and more.

items.q: Is every piece one of a kind?
items.a: Yes. Bagong Buhay is a slow-fashion brand focused on 1/1 pieces, so when one is gone, it’s gone.

items.q: How do I buy a piece?
items.a: In person at markets, or by sending Kim a message on Instagram. You can also send a hold request from the Pieces page.
Each piece is priced individually. Ask on Instagram or send a hold request and Kim will reply with details.
Not right now. Market tables and Instagram DMs are the way to buy.

Bring clothing or a fabric accessory, pick a patch, and sew it on — Kim ran one at the Belmont Street Fair with @craftea.fg.

items.q: Can Kim rework something I already own?
items.a: Maybe. Use the “give it a new life” request form; it’s a request, not a booking, and Kim replies if it’s a fit.
There’s no set turnaround. Kim sews alongside a full-time job, so she batches replies.

items.q: How do I care for an upcycled piece?
items.a: Cold wash inside out or hand wash, line dry, and mend small holes early. Each piece’s care label notes anything special.
Ask first on Instagram — storage is limited, so Kim may not be able to accept everything.
